title: Council pay changes and housing decisions
subtitle: Mooregate redevelopment postponed, housing corporation study, 2026 tax ratios, road and bridge tenders, childcare reimbursement motion defeated.
overview: Council approved a remuneration package for the 2026-2030 term. Annual pay adjustments stay tied to Ontario inflation, capped at 3.0%, and standing committee chair pay rises from $7,401 to $12,901 once the next council takes office. Council also set 2026 property tax ratios, passed the related tax by-laws, and awarded major contracts, including Scheifele Bridge and Fischer-Hallman Road.

On housing, council continued the postponement of the Mooregate redevelopment in Kitchener {{vote:m13}} and directed staff to study a municipal housing corporation, reporting by Q2 2027 {{vote:m24}}. A motion to reimburse elected officials for childcare and caregiving costs was defeated {{vote:m27}}.

Delegates asked for a development charge review, a student transit fare and stronger protection for Wilmot groundwater. Council directed staff to fold the student fare request into the transit review. Public health reminded families of the May 4 immunization record deadline. A motion to extend the meeting failed, and it adjourned at 11:00 p.m.

decisions.detail: Council approved the consultant's recommendation to keep annual pay adjustments tied to Ontario inflation, capped at 3.0%, and to follow any non-union staff freeze or austerity increase.
Council raised standing committee chair remuneration from $7,401 to $12,901 for the 2026-2030 term, to be built into the 2027 budget {{vote:m21}}.

Council continued the postponement of the Mooregate Crescent redevelopment, directed an expression of interest for non-profits and co-operatives on remaining revitalization projects, and asked staff to pursue external funding {{vote:m13}}.
Staff will report to the Community and Health Services Committee by Q2 2027 on whether and how the Region could establish a municipal housing corporation {{vote:m24}}.
Council defeated a motion to draft a policy reimbursing elected officials for childcare and caregiving costs incurred on official duties {{vote:m27}}.
Council set 2026 property class tax ratios, approved preliminary 2025 financial results, and amended the Surplus Allocation Policy.

Council delegated authority to the CAO and Clerk to sign agreements with area municipalities and the tourism marketing corporation on the Region's 10% share of Municipal Accommodation Tax funds {{vote:m11}}.
Council accepted Sierra Infrastructure Inc.'s $19,400,976.10 tender for Scheifele Bridge, Northfield Drive realignment and trunk watermain, subject to a federal Fisheries Act authorization.

debate: Committee chair pay: supporters cited extra workload, scope creep, no recent increase and a comparison with police board members. Others said an increase should come from a consultant or citizen committee rather than being added by council, and one suggested returning it to the consultant. Staff said the consultant had found too little comparable data and would likely charge more. Supporters noted it only applies to the next council.

Staff support: some councillors wanted two proposed positions referred to the 2027 budget instead of directed, citing possible provincial changes to the chair's role. Others said new councillors would not know the workload and that one support person for 15 members is thin. Layered amendments caused confusion, and the vote was restarted and taken one section at a time.

Mooregate: a delegate asked council to reconsider the postponement and urged regular community meetings, a staff contact and communication in several languages. Staff said affected tenants were engaged from late January, that the broader neighbourhood is normally told only after a council decision, and that families were relocated within Region housing.

Housing corporation: the mover said a separate corporation could hold debt and tap financing sources the Region cannot, easing pressure on the Region's debt capacity. Critics pointed to the Region's AAA credit rating, strong results under Building Better Futures, existing non-profit partners and staff workload. Staff noted a dormant corporation already exists, and one councillor said the Region would likely still have to guarantee any debt.

Childcare reimbursement: the mover described caregiving costs as a barrier to serving, and as cost recovery rather than an allowance. Opponents raised cost, public frustration with the cost of government, and a preference for referring it to a consultant. Some said the consultant's review had not covered it.
